**Why it beats LRU:** it ranks keys by how recently they were used *before* their latest access, not just by their latest access.
- **Loops longer than the cache:** LRU gets almost no hits, because it throws away each key just before it comes round again. This policy keeps a stable part of the loop cached, which is where most of the gain comes from.
- **One-off scans:** new keys go into a small separate area first, so a scan pushes out other new keys instead of the hot ones.
- **Adapting to the trace:** a fixed small area (5%) for new keys cost hits on the recency trace (0.80 vs 0.85). So the cache also runs 7 shadow copies with different area sizes (1%–50%) and moves its own size gradually toward whichever copy is getting the most hits.
- **Memory of evicted keys:** it remembers up to 2× capacity of them. 4× gave the same loop result but cost about 0.01 on mixed.
